title: Introduction
text: Add ask-widget to a React application, connect your own backend and customize the interface. ask-widget provides a floating chat interface, a streaming response adapter and headless hooks. Use the supplied widget or compose your own interface around useChat, useSSEStream and useSession.

title: API reference
heading: ChatWidget props
text: ChatWidget props Props are generated from the installed repository source. streamResponse takes precedence over apiUrl and apiToken; no backend props selects demo mode. ChatWidget props Name Type Default Description apiUrl string | undefined — Base URL of your chat API. When provided (without a custom `streamResponse`), the widget will automatically use `useSSEStream` to connect to `<apiUrl>/v1/chat` with an OpenAI-compatible payload. apiToken string | undefined — Bearer token for API authentication. Browser-visible token. Use only a short-lived token scoped to your backend. Keep private provider credentials on the server; frontend environment variables do not conceal secrets. position ChatPosition | undefined bottom-right Position of the floating button and chat panel. theme ChatTheme | undefined dark Color theme preset. colors ChatColors | undefined — Custom color overrides - merged with theme defaults. title string | undefined Ask AI Title shown in the chat panel header. placeholder string | undefined Ask me anything... Placeholder text in the message input. initialMessage string | undefined Hello! How can I help you today? First message displayed when the panel opens. defaultOpen boolean | undefined false Whether the chat panel starts open. labels ChatLabels | undefined — Custom text labels for technical indicators in the UI. persistenceKey string | undefined ask_widget_session The localStorage key used to persist chat history. streamResponse ChatStreamHandler | undefined — Custom response handler - takes full control of streaming. Use this when you need custom fetch logic, auth flows, or a non-SSE backend. When provided, `apiUrl` and `apiToken` are ignored.

title: Architecture
text: Understand the React components, streaming adapter and browser-local persistence. This document describes the high-level architecture and design of @chitrank2050/ask-widget.

title: Architecture
heading: Component Layer
text: Component Layer The main entry point is the ChatWidget component. It renders a floating chat action button and a collapsible chat panel containing: Message List: Renders conversation history as plain text with user/assistant message variants. Input Area: Captures user text and manages the submission state.

title: Architecture
heading: State & Hooks Layer (Headless API)
text: State & Hooks Layer (Headless API) The business logic is decoupled from the UI using custom hooks: useChat: Manages state for the conversation (messages array, loading state, input state). useSSEStream: Connects to the SSE streaming API and streams tokens sequentially. useSession: Manages state persistence across page reloads using localStorage.

title: Architecture
heading: Style & Presentation Layer
text: Style & Presentation Layer The UI is styled using Vanilla CSS with CSS Cascade Layers (@layer) to organize style precedence; CSS layers do not provide selector isolation. Variables are driven by HSL tokens conforming to the neutral zinc palette.

title: Backend and SSE
text: Connect the widget to your own authenticated streaming backend.

title: Backend and SSE
heading: Keep credentials on the server
text: Keep credentials on the server The widget does not host a model or authenticate users. Your server owns provider credentials, user authorization, rate limits and request validation. Browser apiToken values are visible to users; use only short-lived, scoped credentials.

title: Backend and SSE
heading: Built-in adapter
text: Built-in adapter apiUrl is concatenated with /v1/chat. For a same-origin backend, apiUrl="" does not select the adapter: use useSSEStream({ apiUrl: '', path: '/api/chat' }) and pass its streamResponse to ChatWidget. The default body contains messages and stream: true. The default extractor reads choices[0].delta.content from JSON data lines and stops on [DONE]. The path is an ask-widget convention, not a promise that every provider exposes /v1/chat. Adapt path, buildBody and extractChunk to your backend. The parser accepts multiline JSON data events, optional spaces after data:, CR/LF line endings and UTF-8 characters split across network chunks. It also accepts an unterminated final JSON frame at EOF. It does not implement EventSource reconnection or retry fields. useChat supplies history including the current user message exactly once. The default request body uses that history without duplicating the prompt. A standalone adapter call can supply prior history; the adapter appends the prompt unless it is already the last user message.

title: Backend and SSE
heading: Cancel a response
text: Cancel a response Closing the panel, pressing Escape or resetting the conversation cancels the active response. useChat also exposes cancelResponse(). The built-in adapter aborts fetch and cancels its reader. Custom handlers receive an optional third argument with an AbortSignal; pass it to your network request: Existing two-argument handlers continue to work. Their late results are ignored after cancellation, but stopping custom network or server work requires the handler to honor the signal.

title: Backend and SSE
heading: Cross-origin requests
text: Cross-origin requests A remote backend must allow your website origin, POST requests and any required headers in its CORS policy. Do not disable browser security to work around CORS.

title: Backend and SSE
heading: Custom protocols
text: Custom protocols Supply a ChatStreamHandler when your response format differs. It can return text, a promise of text or an async iterable of text chunks. Rendered message content is plain text; Markdown rendering is not part of the current widget.

title: Development

title: Development
heading: Install
text: Install Use Node.js 24.14 or newer and the repository’s pinned pnpm version.

title: Development
heading: Run the website
text: Run the website The website runs at http://localhost:3006. Rebuild the library after editing widget source because the website consumes its emitted package exports.

title: Development
heading: Run the documentation
text: Run the documentation Open http://localhost:4181/ask-widget/. Documentation is built by Monoline Docs independently of Next.js. The /ask-widget/ base preserves existing GitHub Pages URLs. API props are extracted from component source before the documentation build. Restart docs development after changing widget prop declarations to refresh the table.

title: Development
heading: Verify
text: Verify Do not commit docs/dist, package dist or website .next output. The website and documentation have separate deployment targets; docs output is never mounted into the Next.js application.

title: Development
heading: Shared site theme
text: Shared site theme The website and documentation load assets/theme.css for their light and dark color tokens. Edit this file to keep both sites consistent. Website layout styles remain in website/src/app/globals.css; the Docs layout is managed by Monoline Docs.

title: Development
heading: SEO and deployment
text: SEO and deployment The website is deployed independently to https://ask-widget.chitrankagnihotri.com. For Vercel, set the project Root Directory to website and enable source files outside the Root Directory. website/vercel.json builds the library before Next.js and does not build or deploy documentation. Set NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL to that production origin; canonical URLs, social URLs, robots and the sitemap use the same value. Vercel previews emit noindex and disallow crawling. The sitemap omits modification dates until real page revision dates are available. Monoline Docs deploys to https://chitranklabs.github.io/ask-widget/. Its site, base and seo configuration control canonical URLs, social metadata, publisher identity and the sitemap. Keep this base while existing Pages URLs are in use. A project site does not own the host-root /robots.txt; its sitemap is under the project base. The website’s llms.txt links to the Docs Markdown exports. Run pnpm --filter ask-widget-website test:seo against a production build, or set TEST_BASE_URL to an existing local server to check its rendered metadata. Identity synchronization is explicit: run pnpm --filter ask-widget-website sync:identity to refresh the checked-in fallback, then review the result. Normal development and production builds do not rewrite that file from a remote response. build:lib verifies ESM and CommonJS public exports, SSR rendering and both stylesheet aliases after emitting the bundle. CommonJS output uses .cjs because the package is declared as an ES module.

title: Getting started
text: Install the React chat widget and connect your backend. ask-widget is a lightweight React component for adding a streaming AI chat assistant to your developer portfolio. It’s strictly monochrome by default and designed to align with the popular “zinc/neutral” aesthetic.

title: Getting started
heading: Installation
text: Installation

title: Getting started
heading: Registry choice
text: Registry choice Use the npm distribution for the styled React widget; it includes the compiled stylesheet and its styles.css and legacy style.css aliases. The JSR distribution publishes TypeScript source and hooks. JSR does not support CSS module entry points, so the npm stylesheet aliases are not available there. Use npm when following the styled widget examples below.

title: Getting started
heading: Basic Usage
text: Basic Usage To use the widget, render it at the root of your application (or any top-level layout).

title: Getting started
heading: Prerequisites
text: Prerequisites To enable real chat streaming, you’ll need an API that supports Server-Sent Events (SSE). By default, ask-widget expects an OpenAI-compatible endpoint at /v1/chat that accepts a POST request with a messages array in the body. If you don’t have a backend ready yet, the widget will automatically run in demo mode (interactive mocked responses).

title: Getting started
heading: Authentication
text: Authentication Keep private provider API keys on your server. The widget sends requests from the browser, so apiToken is visible to the person using the page. Vite VITE_* and Next.js NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables are public client configuration, not secret storage. Point apiUrl at your own backend, or use streamResponse for an authenticated application endpoint. If your backend requires a browser bearer token, use a short-lived token scoped to that user and endpoint, not a private provider key. Use @chitrank2050/ask-widget/styles.css for the widget stylesheet. The older style.css export remains supported for existing consumers.

title: Standalone hooks
text: Build a custom React chat interface with chat, SSE and persistence hooks. ask-widget is more than just a component-it’s a collection of headless hooks that you can use to build your own completely custom chat interface.

title: Standalone hooks
heading: useChat
text: useChat Manages chat state, message history, and the streaming lifecycle.

title: Standalone hooks
heading: useSSEStream
text: useSSEStream Handles the SSE connection, fetch headers, and token parsing from compatible SSE APIs.

title: Standalone hooks
heading: useSession
text: useSession A simple hook to handle message persistence to localStorage. The hooks must run inside a React component or custom hook. useSession takes a persistence key and optional initial messages; it does not accept an options object. Treat persisted chat history as browser-local data, not secure storage. cancelResponse() stops the current response without clearing completed messages. clearHistory() cancels before resetting. Custom handlers can use their optional abort context as shown in Backend and SSE. Persisted messages are validated before restoration. An unavailable storage API falls back to in-memory state; changing the session key loads that conversation without copying the previous conversation into its storage entry.

title: Next.js and Vite
heading: Next.js App Router
text: Next.js App Router Wrap the interactive widget in a client component and import its stylesheet: Render Assistant from your layout. This example runs demo responses. Connect your own endpoint using the backend guide. Keep private provider keys in server-only environment variables.

title: Next.js and Vite
heading: Vite React
text: Vite React The published package declares React and React DOM 18 or newer as peers. Vite VITE_* variables and Next.js NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables enter browser code; they are suitable for public configuration, not private credentials.

title: Next.js and Vite
heading: Multiple widgets
text: Multiple widgets Give independent conversations distinct persistenceKey values. Otherwise they share the same browser-local history key. Configure positions so launchers do not overlap. The widget does not synchronize conversation state between open tabs.

title: Maintenance and releases
text: Prepare npm and JSR releases, publish verified tags and recover one failed destination.

title: Maintenance and releases
heading: Prepare a release
text: Prepare a release Use Conventional Commits; Lefthook and git-hygiene validate commit messages. Run Release 1 - Prepare PR to calculate the next version and open a release/v<version> branch. The PR updates package.json, jsr.json and the generated CHANGELOG.md together.

title: Maintenance and releases
heading: Finalize
text: Finalize Merging a labeled release PR starts Release 2 - Finalize Tag. The workflow verifies matching versions, runs library tests and types, builds the package and checks its packed contents before creating the tag. A conflicting existing tag fails explicitly; it is never overwritten. npm, JSR and the GitHub release run independently against the verified source commit. npm publishes only the root library, with provenance. JSR publishes its source package using OIDC. GitHub release notes come from git-cliff for that tag. Documentation deployment remains a separate main-branch workflow.

title: Maintenance and releases
heading: Recover a failed destination
text: Recover a failed destination Dispatch Release 2 - Finalize Tag with the exact version and a target: npm, jsr, github or all. Manual recovery requires an existing tag and selects its immutable source commit. If tag creation failed, rerun the original merged-PR build/tag job rather than creating a recovery tag from the current main branch. Published npm versions and existing GitHub releases are retained; JSR skips versions already published. Registry or authentication errors remain visible failures. For a new npm publication, run the workflow from the release tag so the workflow commit and package source match the provenance statement. Recovery from another workflow ref can restore GitHub or JSR, or skip an already published npm version, but cannot publish a new npm version with mismatched provenance. The separate JSR recovery workflow also requires an existing version tag and checks both version files. Do not edit a released version or move a published tag; make a new release for source changes. Publishing still requires npm credentials or its configured trusted publisher, and the JSR repository/OIDC association.

title: Maintenance and releases
heading: Verify locally
text: Verify locally Use deno publish --dry-run --allow-dirty to validate unpublished JSR changes without publishing them. The dirty-tree flag is for this local dry run; CI publishes a clean, verified source checkout. Operational configuration lives in .github/workflows/, the bot action in .github/actions/setup-bot/, lefthook.yml and cliff.toml.

title: Troubleshooting
text: Diagnose stylesheet, streaming, persistence and backend integration problems.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: The widget is unstyled
text: The widget is unstyled Import @chitrank2050/ask-widget/styles.css once in your application. Ensure your build includes CSS assets; importing only headless hooks does not provide your custom interface with styles.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: Demo responses appear instead of real responses
text: Demo responses appear instead of real responses Without a custom streamResponse or a non-empty apiUrl, the component selects the built-in demo. See Backend and SSE for same-origin requests.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: Requests fail or responses stay empty
text: Requests fail or responses stay empty Inspect your browser’s network panel. Check the final URL, response status, CORS headers and your backend’s authentication requirements. The default adapter expects JSON data lines with choices[0].delta.content; change extractChunk for a different payload. Never include credentials when sharing diagnostics.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: History is shared or does not survive a reload
text: History is shared or does not survive a reload Set a distinct persistenceKey per conversation. Browser storage may be disabled or unavailable in private browsing. Saved history is local to the browser and origin; it is not server synchronization or secure storage.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: A custom response continues after closing the panel
text: A custom response continues after closing the panel Close, Escape and reset cancel the active chat request and ignore late results. Pass the handler’s optional context.signal to fetch to stop its network work too. See Cancellation. Existing handlers that ignore the signal cannot have their remote work forcibly stopped by the widget.
